The other two angles at that intersection are 140° each (since 180° - 40° = 140°). This is arithmetically correct and consistent with the stated rules.

This is a standard geometric theorem (converse of corresponding angles postulate) and is internally consistent.

- The text states: "The other angles would measure $140^\circ$". This is correct because the angles adjacent to 40° on a straight line sum to 180°, so 180° - 40° = 140°.
- The text states: "A transversal is a line that intersects two or more other lines in the same plane." This is consistent with the earlier definition.
